+The homepage loads `analytics.js` and POSTs JSON to `/api/analytics`:
+
+```json
+{"events":[{"type":"page_view","timestamp":"2026-11-20T00:00:00.000Z","path":"/"},{"type":"click","timestamp":"2026-11-20T00:00:00.100Z","path":"/","target":{"tag":"a","path":"/menu"}}]}
+```
+
+Configure `ENDPOINT` in `analytics.js` for your collector. This static project does
+not implement a collector; the hosting service must accept these POST requests.
+
+Each click replaces the pending request with the full batch. Batches activate
+after one second without events, within ten seconds of the first event, or at
+50 events / 24 KiB. Individual events are bounded to keep batches below the
+browser's deferred-request quota. Native `fetchLater` handles page exits. Where
+unavailable or quota-limited, a timer and hidden/pagehide listeners send a beacon,
+falling back to a low-priority keepalive fetch. Network failures are best effort
+and are not retried, so analytics cannot create retry storms or block navigation.
+
+Tracking covers the initial page view and delegated clicks, including nested link
+targets and keyboard-generated clicks. Telemetry excludes URL queries, fragments,
+page text, form values, cookies, and persistent user identifiers.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static homepage with a browser-only encrypted delivery-notes demo.
+
+- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
+- `pnpm run build` bundles the browser code to `assets/app.js` (committed so the existing static start command continues to work).
+- `pnpm test` runs cryptographic round-trip and tamper-rejection tests without starting a server.
+
+The browser needs HTTPS or localhost for Web Crypto. No customer note is sent over the network. External fonts and a stock coffee photo load independently of notes.
+
+## Encryption
+
+Default hybrid mode uses noble's ML-KEM-768 + X25519 KEM. Alternatives are ML-KEM-768 alone and ephemeral X25519 agreement. Every note uses a fresh encapsulation, random 32-byte HKDF salt, and random 12-byte AES-GCM nonce. HKDF-SHA-256 derives a non-extractable AES-256 key. AES-GCM authenticates the complete envelope header, including delivery identity, suite, recipient key fingerprint, encapsulation, timestamp, salt, and nonce, with a 128-bit tag. Shared-secret byte arrays are cleared after derivation.
+
+Recipient keys are generated in memory on demand. The encryptor uses the public key; the preview uses the matching private key. Only encrypted envelopes persist in localStorage; plaintext drafts and private keys do not. Reloading loses private keys, so existing ciphertext can be viewed or deleted but cannot be decrypted in the new session. Storage errors retain the draft and report failure. At most 20 notes are retained. Decryption previews use textContent, never HTML.
+
+## Production boundary
+
+This is explicitly a local demo, not a delivery integration or a deployed end-to-end encrypted messaging service. For production, replace session key generation with authenticated recipient public keys from a trusted key directory, bind envelopes to authenticated orders, send ciphertext to an authenticated delivery API, and decrypt only within the intended recipient service. Never ship recipient private keys in client assets. Define rotation, recovery, expiry, replay handling, and access controls with that service. Local storage does not protect against malicious same-origin scripts or an attacker controlling the device. Delivery metadata is authenticated but not encrypted; notes are encrypted. The app does not authenticate who wrote a note.

+import { createRecipient, encryptNote, decryptNote } from './crypto.js';
+const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
+const storageKey = 'daily-grind.encrypted-notes.v1';
+const recipients = new Map();
+const deliveries = { 'next-delivery': 'My next coffee delivery', 'weekly-subscription': 'Weekly coffee subscription', 'gift-delivery': 'A gift delivery' };
+const labels = { hybrid: ['X25519 + ML-KEM-768', 'Classical + post-quantum. Better together.'], postquantum: ['ML-KEM-768', 'A shared secret with post-quantum protection.'], classical: ['X25519', 'Established key agreement. No post-quantum protection.'] };
+let notes = [];
+function status(message, error = false) { $('status').textContent = message; $('status').classList.toggle('error', error); }
+try {
+  const saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(storageKey) || '[]');
+  if (!Array.isArray(saved)) throw new Error();
+  notes = saved.filter(item => item?.header?.version === 1 && Object.hasOwn(labels, item.header.mode) &&
+    typeof item.ciphertext === 'string' && item.ciphertext.length < 10000 &&
+    typeof item.header.id === 'string' && typeof item.header.keyId === 'string' && typeof item.header.created === 'string').slice(0, 20);
+} catch { status('Saved notes could not be loaded. Browser storage may be unavailable.', true); }
+const count = () => { $('char-count').textContent = `${$('note').value.length} / 500`; };
+$('note').addEventListener('input', count);
+document.querySelectorAll('[data-template]').forEach(button => button.addEventListener('click', () => {
+  $('note').value = button.dataset.template; count(); $('note').focus();
+}));
+$('protection').addEventListener('change', () => {
+  const mode = $('protection').value;
+  $('protection-description').textContent = labels[mode][1];
+  $('algorithm-label').textContent = labels[mode][0];
+  $('recommended').hidden = mode !== 'hybrid';
+});
+const dialog = $('info-dialog');
+['how-button', 'privacy-button', 'footer-privacy'].forEach(id => $(id).addEventListener('click', () => dialog.showModal()));
+dialog.querySelectorAll('.dialog-close, .dialog-done').forEach(button => button.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.close()));
+dialog.addEventListener('click', event => { if (event.target === dialog) {
+  const box = dialog.getBoundingClientRect();
+  if (event.clientX < box.left || event.clientX > box.right || event.clientY < box.top || event.clientY > box.bottom) dialog.close();
+}});
+function element(tag, className, content) {
+  const el = document.createElement(tag); if (className) el.className = className;
+  if (content !== undefined) el.textContent = content; return el;
+}
+function persist(next) { localStorage.setItem(storageKey, JSON.stringify(next)); notes = next; }
+function renderNotes() {
+  const list = $('notes-list');
+  if (!notes.length) { list.replaceChildren(element('div', 'empty-state', 'No encrypted notes yet. Add a little care to your next delivery above.')); return; }
+  list.replaceChildren();
+  notes.forEach(envelope => {
+    const { header } = envelope;
+    const recipient = recipients.get(header.mode);
+    const available = recipient?.keyId === header.keyId;
+    const card = element('article', 'saved-note');
+    const top = element('div', 'saved-top');
+    top.append(element('strong', '', deliveries[header.delivery] || 'Coffee delivery'));
+    const time = new Date(header.created);
+    top.append(element('small', '', Number.isNaN(time.getTime()) ? 'Saved note' : time.toLocaleString(undefined, { dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' })));
+    const remove = element('button', '', 'Delete'); remove.type = 'button';
+    remove.addEventListener('click', () => {
+      try { persist(notes.filter(note => note !== envelope)); renderNotes(); status('Encrypted note deleted from this device.'); }
+      catch { status('Could not delete this note. Browser storage is unavailable.', true); }
+    }); top.append(remove); card.append(top);
+    card.append(element('p', 'saved-meta', `${labels[header.mode][0]} · AES-256-GCM · ${available ? 'Key available in this session' : 'Session key expired — unable to decrypt'}`));
+    const actions = element('div', 'note-actions');
+    if (available) {
+      const reveal = element('button', '', 'Decrypt preview'); reveal.type = 'button'; let shown = false;
+      const preview = element('p', 'decrypted'); preview.hidden = true;
+      reveal.addEventListener('click', async () => {
+        if (shown) { preview.textContent = ''; preview.hidden = true; shown = false; reveal.textContent = 'Decrypt preview'; return; }
+        try { preview.textContent = await decryptNote(envelope, recipient); preview.hidden = false; shown = true; reveal.textContent = 'Hide preview'; }
+        catch { status('This note could not be authenticated. It may have been altered.', true); }
+      }); actions.append(reveal); card.append(actions, preview);
+    }
+    const details = element('details'); details.append(element('summary', '', 'View encrypted envelope'));
+    details.append(element('code', 'ciphertext', JSON.stringify(envelope, null, 2))); card.append(details); list.append(card);
+  });
+}
+$('note-form').addEventListener('submit', async event => {
+  event.preventDefault();
+  const note = $('note').value.trim();
+  if (!note) { status('Add a delivery instruction before encrypting.', true); $('note').focus(); return; }
+  if (!globalThis.crypto?.subtle) { status('Encryption needs a secure connection (HTTPS or localhost).', true); return; }
+  if (notes.length >= 20) { status('You have 20 saved notes. Delete one before saving another.', true); return; }
+  const mode = $('protection').value;
+  const button = $('save-button'); button.disabled = true; button.querySelector('span').textContent = 'Encrypting your note…';
+  status('Establishing a fresh shared secret in your browser…');
+  try {
+    if (!recipients.has(mode)) recipients.set(mode, await createRecipient(mode));
+    const envelope = await encryptNote(note, recipients.get(mode), $('delivery-select').value);

+    status('Note encrypted and saved on this device. Nothing was sent to a courier.');
+  } catch { status('Your note could not be saved securely. Check browser storage and try again. Your draft is still here.', true); }
+  finally { button.disabled = false; button.querySelector('span').textContent = 'Encrypt & save note'; }
+});
+renderNotes();

+import { ml_kem768 } from '@noble/post-quantum/ml-kem.js';
+import { ml_kem768_x25519 } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+import { x25519 } from '@noble/curves/ed25519.js';
+
+const classical = {
+  keygen: () => x25519.keygen(),
+  encapsulate(publicKey) {
+    const ephemeral = x25519.keygen();
+    try {
+      return { cipherText: ephemeral.publicKey, sharedSecret: x25519.getSharedSecret(ephemeral.secretKey, publicKey) };
+    } finally { ephemeral.secretKey.fill(0); }
+  },
+  decapsulate: (cipherText, secretKey) => x25519.getSharedSecret(secretKey, cipherText),
+};
+export const suites = { hybrid: ml_kem768_x25519, postquantum: ml_kem768, classical };
+const encode = new TextEncoder();
+export const toBase64 = bytes => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
+const fromBase64 = text => Uint8Array.from(atob(text), char => char.charCodeAt(0));
+export async function createRecipient(mode) {
+  if (!Object.hasOwn(suites, mode)) throw new Error('Unknown protection level');
+  const keys = suites[mode].keygen();
+  const keyId = toBase64(new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', keys.publicKey)));
+  return { ...keys, keyId, mode };
+}
+async function deriveKey(sharedSecret, salt, header) {
+  try {
+    const material = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', sharedSecret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+    return await crypto.subtle.deriveKey({ name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt,
+      info: await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', encode.encode('daily-grind/delivery-notes/v1/' + JSON.stringify(header))) }, material,
+      { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+  } finally { sharedSecret.fill(0); }
+}
+export async function encryptNote(note, recipient, delivery) {
+  if (!note.trim() || note.length > 500) throw new Error('Write a note between 1 and 500 characters.');
+  const { cipherText, sharedSecret } = suites[recipient.mode].encapsulate(recipient.publicKey);
+  const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));
+  const salt = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
+  const header = { version: 1, mode: recipient.mode, keyId: recipient.keyId, delivery,
+    id: crypto.randomUUID(), created: new Date().toISOString(), encapsulation: toBase64(cipherText),
+    salt: toBase64(salt), iv: toBase64(iv) };
+  const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, salt, header);
+  const plaintext = encode.encode(note);
+  try {
+    const ciphertext = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, tagLength: 128,
+      additionalData: encode.encode(JSON.stringify(header)) }, key, plaintext);
+    return { header, ciphertext: toBase64(new Uint8Array(ciphertext)) };
+  } finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+}
+export async function decryptNote(envelope, recipient) {
+  const { header, ciphertext } = envelope;
+  if (header.version !== 1 || header.mode !== recipient.mode || header.keyId !== recipient.keyId)
+    throw new Error('The recipient key is unavailable for this note.');
+  const sharedSecret = suites[header.mode].decapsulate(fromBase64(header.encapsulation), recipient.secretKey);
+  const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, fromBase64(header.salt), header);
+  const plaintext = await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: fromBase64(header.iv), tagLength: 128,
+    additionalData: encode.encode(JSON.stringify(header)) }, key, fromBase64(ciphertext));
+  const bytes = new Uint8Array(plaintext);
+  try { return new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(bytes); }
+  finally { bytes.fill(0); }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+import test from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { createRecipient, encryptNote, decryptNote, toBase64 } from './crypto.js';
+for (const mode of ['hybrid', 'postquantum', 'classical']) {
+  test(`${mode}: Unicode round trip, fresh randomness, no plaintext in envelope`, async () => {
+    const recipient = await createRecipient(mode);
+    const note = 'Gate code 8492. Quiet delivery, please ☕';
+    const first = await encryptNote(note, recipient, 'next-delivery');
+    const second = await encryptNote(note, recipient, 'next-delivery');
+    assert.equal(await decryptNote(first, recipient), note);
+    assert.notEqual(first.ciphertext, second.ciphertext);
+    assert.notEqual(first.header.iv, second.header.iv);
+    assert.notEqual(first.header.encapsulation, second.header.encapsulation);
+    assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(first).includes('8492'));
+    assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(first).includes('secretKey'));
+  });
+  test(`${mode}: rejects ciphertext, metadata, encapsulation tampering and wrong recipient`, async () => {
+    const recipient = await createRecipient(mode);
+    const envelope = await encryptNote('Side door code 1234', recipient, 'next-delivery');
+    const corrupt = value => {
+      const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(value), c => c.charCodeAt(0)); bytes[0] ^= 1; return toBase64(bytes);
+    };
+    const ciphertext = structuredClone(envelope); ciphertext.ciphertext = corrupt(ciphertext.ciphertext);
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote(ciphertext, recipient));
+    for (const field of ['delivery', 'id', 'created', 'iv', 'salt', 'encapsulation']) {
+      const modified = structuredClone(envelope);
+      modified.header[field] = ['iv', 'salt', 'encapsulation'].includes(field) ? corrupt(modified.header[field]) : 'altered';
+      await assert.rejects(decryptNote(modified, recipient));
+    }
+    const other = await createRecipient(mode);
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote(envelope, other));
+    // Also reject the wrong private key even if the caller copies the key identifier.
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote(envelope, { ...other, keyId: recipient.keyId }));
+  });
+}
+test('invalid input fails closed', async () => {
+  await assert.rejects(createRecipient('unknown'));
+  await assert.rejects(createRecipient('__proto__'));
+  const recipient = await createRecipient('hybrid');
+  await assert.rejects(encryptNote('   ', recipient, 'next-delivery'));
+  await assert.rejects(encryptNote('x'.repeat(501), recipient, 'next-delivery'));
+});

Curious about what’s happening under the hood?A little more about smallpt

Each pixel is an average of many randomly sampled light paths. Rays bounce through a Cornell box, reflecting off the mirror sphere, refracting through the glass sphere, and picking up color from the walls before reaching the ceiling light. More samples make the image less noisy.

The original C++ rendering algorithm is compiled with Emscripten into WebAssembly and runs in a dedicated Web Worker. Completed rows are sent to this canvas as they render. Randomizing changes the two wall colors and both sphere colors while preserving their materials.

+# Elsewhere
+
+A responsive, static travel landing page. Open `index.html` through your existing static hosting workflow. No build step or dependencies are required. The primary buttons open a working escape finder; destination cards preselect a preference.
+
+## Experiment integration
+
+The head hides only the experiment region before it can paint. `experiment.js` loads `https://cdn.example.com/experiment-sdk.js` in a hidden same-origin staging iframe containing `#hero-experiment`, `#hero-title`, `#hero-description`, and `#hero-cta`. The SDK can modify those DOM nodes normally.
+
+**Required SDK completion contract:** after all DOM mutations are complete, call `window.experimentReady()` or dispatch `experiment:ready` on the staging window/document. This explicit signal matters because a script's load event does not imply asynchronous experiments have finished. The assigned local variant is also available as `window.experimentVariant` in staging.
+
+On completion, the entire staged region is copied into the visible page synchronously and revealed. On network error or after 1.8 seconds, a locally assigned A/B variant is applied before reveal. Assignment is retained in localStorage; blocked storage falls back to B. The staging iframe is destroyed in either case, preventing late SDK writes from changing a visible fallback. Parent-level delegated CTA handlers work after replacement. No JavaScript users receive the static page via a noscript visibility override.
+
+The supplied CDN URL is a placeholder. A production SDK must implement the completion contract and support the staging document; SDKs that require direct top-level document access need an adapter. Load success alone never reveals the control. No SDK behavior or live endpoint availability has been verified.
+
+Run `node experiment.test.cjs` to check the reveal lifecycle with a lightweight DOM harness. No browser or development server is needed.

+# Rewards registration integration
+
+The static site includes a three-step registration client. It does not include an account database or pretend to create accounts. No personal data is sent until the HTTPS, same-origin CSRF endpoint succeeds. Without JavaScript, registration is disabled with an explanation because the static HTML cannot carry a server-issued token.
+

+# Script performance monitoring
+
+`script-performance.js` automatically observes animation frames longer than 50ms,
+including buffered frames from before it loaded. It records timestamp, page,
+frame duration, blocking duration, and script attribution where available.
+
+Inspect the monitor from the developer console:
+
+```js
+scriptPerformance.supported // browser supports long-animation-frame entries
+scriptPerformance.monitoring // observer started successfully
+scriptPerformance.getHistory() // oldest to newest; detached copies
+console.table(scriptPerformance.getSlowScripts()) // cumulative script time >= 100ms
+console.table(scriptPerformance.getSlowScripts(0)) // all attributed scripts
+scriptPerformance.clearHistory()
+```
+
+History stays on this device and origin in localStorage under
+`daily-grind:slow-frames:v1`; no data is sent to a server. The latest 100 frames
+are retained across reloads, with the 10 longest script invocations per frame.
+Aggregates cover only this retained history and count invocations, not frames.
+URLs omit query strings and fragments. Storage writes are batched for one second
+and flushed when the page is hidden or exited. If storage is unavailable, history
+remains in memory (`scriptPerformance.persistenceAvailable` becomes false after
+a failed write).
+
+Unsupported browsers skip observation but can still inspect saved history.
+Frames without script attribution are retained; rendering, cross-origin code,
+and other browser work can contribute to delays. Attribution shows contributors,
+not proof that a particular script alone caused the delay. No timing loops or
+synthetic slow scripts run on the page.
+
+Run the automated observer/storage tests with `npm test`. No server is required.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+The static homepage loads a self-hosted INP monitor from `assets/inp.js`.
+Rebuild it after changing `src/` or updating dependencies:
+
+```sh
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm build
+pnpm test
+```
+
+Commit and deploy `assets/inp.js` and its generated license file alongside
+`index.html`. No runtime CDN or server is needed for the monitor itself.
+
+## Connect field collection
+
+The script's `data-inp-endpoint="/analytics"` in `index.html` is the collector
+URL. **This static repository does not implement a collector.** Configure your
+hosting platform to route POST `/analytics` to your analytics service, or replace
+the attribute with an existing collector URL. Until that is configured, reports
+will be attempted but will not be stored. The collector must accept a JSON object
+in a `text/plain` POST body, return a successful response, and persist the fields
+below. Allow the destination in CSP `connect-src` when deploying with a CSP.
+An empty endpoint disables collection.
+
+Reports use `navigator.sendBeacon`, with `fetch({keepalive:true})` when Beacon
+is unavailable, throws, or rejects queueing. Delivery is best effort; no retries
+or persistent client storage are used. Beacon success only means queued, so
+server failures cannot be detected or retried by this client.
+
+`web-vitals/attribution` calculates INP across the page lifetime and flushes on
+visibility becoming hidden, including navigation away. It continues observing
+when the visitor returns and starts a new metric after a back/forward cache
+restore. It does not upload every input, report pages with no interactions, or
+invent measurements on browsers without the required Event Timing support.
+All measured ratings are sent, so good visits remain in the denominator.
+
+## Report contract (schemaVersion 1)
+
+- `page`: fixed `daily-grind-home`; `name`: `INP`.
+- `id`, `sequence`, `reportedAt`: upsert by metric `id`, keeping the highest
+  `sequence` (which increases within a document). A later report updates a visit,
+  rather than representing a second visit. Do not sum `value` or average updates.
+- `value`, `delta`, `rating`, `navigationType`: the library's metric fields.
+  `value` is the current page INP, not every slow interaction. All times are ms.
+- `interactionTarget`: stable `data-inp-target` label on homepage links;
+  `interactionType`, `interactionTime`, `nextPaintTime`, `loadState`: context.
+  Relative timestamps share the document's performance time origin.
+- `inputDelay`, `processingDuration`, `presentationDelay`: the three INP phases.
+- `longestScript`: URL, function, character offset, invocation type, timings,
+  overlapping duration and the INP `subpart` identified by the library.
+- `scripts`: up to ten scripts overlapping the interaction, sorted by overlapping
+  duration; `scriptsTruncated` indicates omitted entries. Full script `duration`
+  and `intersectingDuration` differ when a script straddles the interaction.
+- `forcedStyleDuration`, `forcedLayoutDuration` on script summaries: synchronous
+  style/layout work. `forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration` is the combined fallback.
+- `renderStyleDuration`, `renderLayoutDuration`: sums of available separate
+  rendering-phase timings across overlapping long animation frames. These are
+  full-frame timings and can extend outside the interaction; do not add them to
+  the INP phase durations or combined library totals.
+- `totalScriptDuration`, `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration`, `totalPaintDuration`,
+  `totalUnattributedDuration`: the library's breakdown of the interaction window.
+  Combined style/layout includes synchronous forced work and rendering work;
+  script totals exclude forced style/layout to avoid double counting.
+- `longAnimationFrameCount`: number of overlapping frames. Unsupported or absent
+  attribution is `null`/empty, not zero. INP and its phases still work without
+  Long Animation Frames. Separate style/layout fields are feature-dependent;
+  use the combined totals when they are unavailable.
+
+Script attribution is diagnostic evidence rather than a complete trace: LoAF
+reports frames over 50ms and scripts over 5ms, and cross-origin script details
+may be unavailable. No input values, page query strings, text content, DOM nodes,
+or raw performance entries are serialized; script URL queries and fragments are
+removed. Keep target labels static and free of customer information.
+
+In analytics, calculate p75 of the latest `value` per `id` (good: <=200ms;
+needs improvement: >200–500ms; poor: >500ms). For slow visits, group by target,
+dominant INP phase, script URL/function and `longestScript.subpart`. High forced
+layout suggests layout thrashing; high rendering style/layout points to the
+rendering phase. Track missing attribution separately from measured zero costs.
+
+Validation uses Node tests for serialization, missing API data, attribution
+boundaries, privacy filtering, bounded payloads and transport fallbacks. The
+build bundles only client code; no browser or server is required for these checks.
+
+References: [web-vitals](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals) and
+[Chrome's INP attribution guidance](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides/performance/identify-inp-causes).

+# The Daily Grind
+
+The static homepage loads field INP instrumentation from `assets/inp.mjs`.
+No build is required. Run `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` for the telemetry checks.
+
+## Connect field reporting
+
+Set the `rum-endpoint` meta tag in `index.html` to an actual analytics collector
+URL, for example `/telemetry/web-vitals`. This repository has no backend, so a
+collector is not provided and network reporting stays disabled until configured.
+The collector must accept JSON POST requests, preferably respond with 204, and
+store the report. For an external collector, configure CORS for this site's
+origin and permit it in the site's CSP `connect-src`. Apply your site's consent
+policy before enabling collection.
+
+Reports use `navigator.sendBeacon` with a `fetch` keepalive fallback. Delivery
+is best effort, with no retries or persistent storage. Reports also dispatch a
+`daily-grind:inp` window event with the same JSON-safe payload in `event.detail`;
+an existing analytics integration can subscribe instead of using the meta tag.
+Install that listener before the module executes if using this integration.
+
+All measured visits report good and slow INP candidates with value, rating,
+metric ID, navigation type, a static interaction label and three phases:
+input delay, processing duration and presentation delay. Values are milliseconds.
+Reports above 200 ms also include the longest intersecting script (source URL,
+function name, source character offset, intersecting duration and INP phase),
+plus up to five overlapping Long Animation Frames and eight scripts per frame.
+Frames and scripts are ordered by duration, with original counts retained to
+indicate truncation. Rendering totals distinguish script time, style/layout,
+paint and unattributed time. Script entries include forced style/layout time.
+The library computes these totals; do not sum frame or script durations as INP.
+Frames provide context; scripts within them may extend beyond the interaction.
+
+The library manages buffered observations, lifecycle reporting when the page
+becomes hidden, and back/forward cache restores. `reportAllChanges` also emits
+updates as the INP candidate changes. Upsert by metric `id`, preserving the `value`
+with the highest `sequence` to handle out-of-order delivery; do not count every
+update as a separate visit or sum values.
+Compute field p75 from the final value for each metric ID. Visits with no
+qualifying interactions do not produce an INP report. INP is the library's
+page-level metric, not a log of every slow click.
+
+Detailed attribution depends on Event Timing and Long Animation Frame browser
+support. Capability flags and null totals distinguish missing data from zero
+work. Frames below 50 ms and scripts below 5 ms can be absent from LoAF data;
+cross-origin script attribution may be limited. Missing attribution is not
+evidence that scripts or rendering caused no delay.
+
+Only explicitly authored `data-inp-target` labels identify interactions. The
+payload excludes DOM nodes, text, input values, page queries and fragments;
+script URL queries/fragments and non-HTTP URLs are discarded. Source URLs and
+function names are bounded, and detailed entries are capped to keep reports
+small. No cookies or persistent identifiers are added by this instrumentation.
+
+## Vendored library
+
+`assets/vendor/web-vitals-attribution-6.2.3.mjs` and its source map are the
+unmodified attribution ESM distribution from Google's `web-vitals` npm package
+6.2.3, with its Apache 2.0 license alongside it. The tarball was checked against
+the npm registry's SHA-512 integrity before copying. This keeps runtime monitoring
+local and avoids a CDN dependency or a new application build step.
+
+Upstream API documentation: https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals#attribution-build

+# The Daily Grind account UI
+
+Open `index.html` for the account screen. The original coffee landing page is preserved in `home.html` and its My Account link opens the account screen.
+
+## Demo mode
+
+This repository is a static site with no authentication server or credential database. The default screen displays a labeled demo account with three sample passkeys. Renames and deletions persist in this browser's local storage. Demo credentials are **never** sent to a real browser authenticator. Clear the `daily-grind-demo-passkeys-v1` local storage entry to reset the sample account.
+
+## Connect the authenticated account API
+
+Set `window.DAILY_GRIND_ACCOUNT_API = '/api'` in a script before `account.js` loads. The adapter sends same-origin session cookies and expects:
+
+- `GET /api/credentials`: return `{ rpId, userId, credentials }`.
+- `PUT /api/credential/:id`: accept `{ "name": "My laptop" }`, persist the nickname, and return a successful response.
+- `DELETE /api/credential/:id`: delete the credential and return a successful response.
+
+A credential has this shape:
+
+```json
+{
+  "id": "Y3JlZC0x",
+  "name": "My laptop",
+  "provider": "iCloud Keychain",
+  "device": "laptop",
+  "registeredAt": 1791763200000,
+  "lastUsedAt": 1795132800000,
+  "current": true
+}
+```
+
+Use raw epoch milliseconds for dates; `lastUsedAt` and `current` are optional. Device icon hints are `laptop`, `phone`, and `usb`, with a generic key fallback. Provider labels should come from registration AAGUID metadata; unknown providers receive a neutral fallback. `userId` and credential IDs must be actual unpadded Base64URL values. `rpId` must be the server's registration RP ID, including when it differs from the account page's hostname.
+
+Every endpoint must require a signed-in session and restrict operations to that user's credentials. Enforce CSRF/origin protection and validate names on the server. Configure credential management according to the account's recovery policy before permitting deletion of its last sign-in method. Replace the illustrative account identity and ancillary account panels with authenticated account data when integrating.
+
+In API mode, the client fetches authoritative records after changes and calls `PublicKeyCredential.signalAllAcceptedCredentials()` on initial load and after deletion. Feature detection and nonfatal error handling preserve account management when the Signal API is unavailable. Nickname changes only update the account label; they do not change the account username or password manager label.
+
+## Checks
+
+`pnpm test` runs automated DOM tests without starting a web server or opening a browser. No build step is required for this static site.

+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+Audited November 20, 2026. Scope: the complete supplied repository, which contains one static HTML page. Verification uses source analysis, asset inspection, and a dependency-free Node audit. No browser, development/preview server, or server entrypoint was used. There is no build script to run.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Outcome |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | Hero was discoverable only through inline CSS, with no fetch-priority signal. | Replaced background URL with an HTML `picture` and one eager, high-priority image. The parser can discover the image directly. No redundant preload. |
+| Image transfer | Every device received the same third-party 1,350px JPEG. | Self-hosted 480/800/1,350px AVIF and WebP variants, plus JPEG fallback. Only one selected image downloads. Original photo and center-cover composition retained. |
+| Connection overhead | Critical image required a connection to images.unsplash.com. | All runtime resources are same-origin; no external fonts or scripts. |
+| Responsive selection | No viewport/density-aware image choices. | Width descriptors and `sizes` account for both viewport width and the extra source width required by `object-fit: cover` on tall screens. Variants cap at the original source resolution, avoiding artificial upscaling. |
+| CLS | Existing CSS background already had a reserved hero height. | Retained reserved space; added intrinsic image dimensions, a minimum hero height, and stable small-viewport sizing with a `vh` fallback. System fonts avoid late font swaps. These are safeguards, not a measured CLS improvement. |
+| Mobile interaction | Non-wrapping navigation and a 250px grid minimum could exceed narrow layouts. | Navigation and links wrap, grid tracks can shrink, heading scales, navigation targets have 44px minimum height, and mobile navigation no longer stays over content while scrolling. |
+| INP | No JavaScript, timers, input handlers, hydration, synchronous computation, or layout-thrashing code exists. | Preserved native links and zero runtime JavaScript. Added keyboard focus feedback and reduced-motion support. No slow handler was found or claimed fixed. |
+| CSS/DOM | Small inline stylesheet, shallow DOM, three text-only cards. | Kept CSS inline to avoid another blocking request. No stylesheet loader, rendering containment, or service worker added: these would add complexity without a demonstrated benefit here. |
+| Repeat visits | Hosting cache policy is not provided. | Content-hashed image filenames and `_headers` rules allow one-year immutable asset caching and revalidated HTML on compatible static hosts. Actual header delivery remains host-dependent. |
+| Regression protection | No performance checks existed. | `npm run audit:performance` checks local asset existence, content hashes, image priority/dimensions, responsive markup, remote subresources, blocking resources, and transfer-size budgets. |
+
+## Measured asset sizes
+
+These are file sizes, not browser timing or field Core Web Vitals measurements. The original URL returned a JPEG during this audit; Unsplash format negotiation may differ by client.
+
+| Resource | Before | After | Reduction |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Hero, 480px AVIF | 157,968 B fixed JPEG | 6,633 B | 95.8% |
+| Hero, 800px AVIF | 157,968 B fixed JPEG | 13,518 B | 91.4% |
+| Hero, 1,350px AVIF | 157,968 B fixed JPEG | 30,484 B | 80.7% |
+| Hero, 1,350px WebP | 157,968 B fixed JPEG | 46,700 B | 70.4% |
+| Hero, JPEG fallback | 157,968 B | 97,098 B | 38.5% |
+| HTML, uncompressed | 4,708 B | 6,431 B | +1,723 B |
+| HTML, local gzip estimate | 1,735 B | 2,259 B | +524 B |
+| Runtime JavaScript | 0 B | 0 B | Unchanged |
+
+The extra HTML supplies format fallbacks, responsive source selection, and responsive styling. Image variants are alternatives, not cumulative page-transfer costs. Actual selection depends on viewport, pixel density, browser capabilities, and browser heuristics. Gzip size is an offline estimate; it does not establish that the host serves compression.
+
+## Validation
+
+- `npm run audit:performance`: passed. Budgets: HTML <=10 KiB; each AVIF <=35,000 B, WebP <=50,000 B, JPEG <=100,000 B.
+- ImageMagick decoded all seven assets successfully. All six responsive width descriptors match decoded image dimensions.
+- Compared original and updated anchor destinations: all 13 are preserved.
+- `git diff --check`: passed.
+
+No LCP/INP/CLS scores, Lighthouse results, TTFB measurements, or visual verification are claimed. Source and byte checks cannot measure browser rendering or interaction latency.
+
+## Deployment and measurement follow-through
+
+1. Publish `index.html`, `assets/`, and `_headers` together. `_headers` is supported by hosts such as Cloudflare Pages and Netlify; the existing `statikk` start command is not demonstrated to consume it. +# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+Audited 2026-11-20. Scope: the supplied static homepage, its assets, CSS, navigation, and package configuration. No browser, development server, preview server, or server entrypoint was used. There is no build pipeline or application JavaScript in this repository.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Change / outcome |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | The hero was a CSS background; its request depended on CSS processing and had no priority hint. | A native HTML image exposes the resource to the preload scanner and uses `fetchpriority="high"` and `loading="eager"`. |
+| Image transfer | Every viewport requested a remote 1350px photo. | Three local, compressed WebP candidates with `srcset` and `sizes="100vw"`; the browser selects by viewport, pixel density, and its own heuristics. |
+| Connection overhead | Rendering the hero required a connection to `images.unsplash.com`. | Rendering now uses only the site's origin. No external fonts, CSS, scripts, or images remain. |
+| Layout stability | The hero already reserved height, but `vh` can resize with mobile browser controls. | Retained the reserved hero area, added a minimum height and stable `svh` with `vh` fallback; the image has intrinsic dimensions and fills the reserved box. |
+| Small-screen interactions | Navigation could overflow because it could not wrap; navigation and footer links had small targets. | Navigation wraps without JavaScript, links have a 44px minimum height, headings scale down, and the card grid can shrink below 250px. |
+| Main-thread work / INP | No scripts, handlers, hydration, timers, or synchronous application work exist. | Preserved native links and zero JavaScript. Added visible keyboard focus and reduced-motion support. There was no code-level long-task bottleneck to remove. |
+| Regression prevention | No performance checks existed. | Added `npm run audit:performance` with HTML/image budgets, content-fingerprint checks, LCP loading checks, and checks against new script, font, CSS, or third-party rendering dependencies. |
+
+The existing short inline stylesheet and system font stack remain appropriate: they avoid additional render-blocking requests. The page has only 49 HTML elements, so DOM virtualization, deferred rendering, and framework code splitting would add complexity without a demonstrated benefit. No preload was added: the native image is already present early in this small HTML document, and no extra resource request is needed to discover it.
+
+## Measured static results
+
+The original image was fetched using the exact URL from the original stylesheet. These are file sizes, not browser timing measurements; the remote response can vary with content negotiation or future upstream changes.
+
+| Resource | Before | After | Reduction |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Hero, 640px candidate | 157,968 B fixed image | 32,260 B | 79.6% |
+| Hero, 960px candidate | 157,968 B fixed image | 56,230 B | 64.4% |
+| Hero, 1350px candidate | 157,968 B | 100,086 B | 36.6% |
+| HTML, uncompressed | 4,708 B | 6,111 B | Increased 1,403 B |
+| HTML, gzip estimate | 1,735 B | 2,113 B | Increased 378 B |
+| Application JavaScript | 0 B | 0 B | Preserved |
+| Third-party rendering origins | 1 | 0 | Removed |
+
+Only one responsive image candidate is normally downloaded. A high-density mobile device may select a larger candidate, so the smallest-image savings do not apply to every mobile visit. The maximum image width remains 1350px, matching the original maximum resolution. Compressed HTML figures use local gzip and do not prove that the production host enables compression.
+
+## Verification
+
+- `npm run audit:performance`: passes. Budgets: HTML ≤10 KB raw / ≤3 KB gzipped; images ≤40 KB at 640px, ≤70 KB at 960px, and ≤120 KB at 1350px.
+- ImageMagick `identify`: validates all three WebP files and their dimensions (640×427, 960×640, 1350×900).
+- Python standard-library HTML parser: balanced HTML nesting; 49 elements and 13 navigation links inspected.
+- `git diff --check`: passes.
+
+The regression command requires only Node.js and can run in CI without a dependency installation, server, or browser. Its deliberately narrow checks suit this single static page; update its budgets explicitly if product requirements change.
+
+## Remaining production checks and limits
+
+Actual LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, and TTFB were not measured. Static analysis cannot establish a Core Web Vitals pass or a Lighthouse score. Production field data is required to validate the results; use the 75th percentile, split by mobile and desktop, with targets of LCP ≤2.5 seconds, INP ≤200 milliseconds, and CLS ≤0.1. INP needs qualifying real interactions and cannot be inferred from the absence of JavaScript.
+
+Production cache headers, compression, TLS, CDN behavior, redirects, server latency, and real navigation responses cannot be established from these files. Configure the host to compress HTML, revalidate HTML on repeat visits, and serve the content-fingerprinted `/assets/*.webp` files with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Asset content changes must update the fingerprint and HTML references together. No host-specific header file was added because no deployment target is defined here.
+
+All 13 links point to paths whose page implementations are absent from this repository. They may be served by the production platform, but this checkout cannot establish that. Their response latency, account/logout behavior, ordering flow, and any downstream interaction slowness remain outside the available source. Existing destinations were preserved.
+
+## Asset provenance and guidance
+
+The hero retains the original Unsplash photo, downloaded from its original [image endpoint](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085) with explicit WebP encoding, quality 60, and widths of 640, 960, and 1350 pixels. No image generation was used. Image fetching is a one-time preparation step; the live page has no Unsplash dependency.
+
+Implementation follows Google's guidance on [LCP discovery and priority](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp), [responsive image sizing and dimensions](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides/performance/performance), and [Core Web Vitals field thresholds](https://web.dev/articles/vitals).
